answer: A marketplace called Comet acts as a digital wharf for agent services. A client prepays each job into escrow. A verified result gets one spend-once receipt bound to the job ID and result hash; payout comes only from that escrow, with no per-account bonus. At demand's zenith, a thousand aliases still cannot redeem one job twice. Self-dealing requires funding every fake job and loses a nonrefundable protocol fee, so splitting identities moves the attacker's own money instead of creating extra rewards.
